true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage origin check uses substring match instead of equality

`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl. For `discourseUrl = "http://discourse.example.com/"` an attacker page at `http://discourse.example.co` (a prefix) passes the check. The impact is limited to controlling the iframe height, but the check should compare the parsed origin of discourseUrl for equality with e.origin.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Unescaped URL interpolated into raw-HTML post footer enables stored XSS TopicEmbed.import appends `#{url}` to the contents without any HTML escaping, and the resulting post is stored with cook_method raw_html, so cooked == raw with no sanitization. The `url` reaches this code from the user-controlled `embed_url` query parameter (EmbedController#best -> RetrieveTopic job -> TopicRetriever -> import_remote). TopicRetriever only checks that the URI host equals embeddable_host; the path may contain `'` (a legal URI character), so a value such as `http://host/x'onmouseover='alert(1)` injects an attribute into the anchor. If the embeddable host serves any 200 page for that path, the payload is stored in a public post authored by the embed_by user and executes for every forum visitor and in the embed iframe. The url (and the title) must be HTML-escaped before interpolation.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Stray `end if` in ERB only compiles by accident

`<%- end if %>` emits the Ruby `end if` with no condition; it only parses because ERB appends the next template text as `@output_buffer.safe_append=...` on the following line, which becomes the modifier-if condition. Any reformatting (e.g. putting another `<% %>` tag directly after, or a different ERB handler) turns this into a SyntaxError and the embed page will 500. It should be `<%- end %>`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
`i.content.scrub` raises for standard RSS items and on Ruby < 2.1

SimpleRSS exposes `content` only for Atom feeds; plain RSS 2.0 items expose `description` (and `content_encoded` for the content module), so `i.content` is nil for most RSS feeds and `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError, aborting the whole poll (retry: false). Additionally, `String#scrub` only exists from Ruby 2.1; on Ruby 2.0 (current at the time of this code) it raises NoMethodError even for Atom feeds. Fall back to `i.content_encoded || i.description` and guard the encoding cleanup.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
Already-committed migration modified to add force: true

An existing migration is edited to use `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. Editing a migration that has already been applied elsewhere is unsafe: anyone who re-runs it (e.g. via `db:migrate:redo` or a fresh schema rebuild from migrations) will have the existing top_topics table silently dropped along with its data. The same `force: true` is used in the new topic_embeds migration; a new migration should not need it.

Concurrent imports of the same URL hit the unique index after creating a topic

import checks `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and later `TopicEmbed.create!`. The hourly PollFeed job and a RetrieveTopic job (which itself invokes PollFeed) can import the same URL concurrently; the second one creates a topic and post, then `create!` raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique on the unique embed_url index, rolling back the transaction and propagating an exception that aborts the rest of the feed import. Rescue RecordNotUnique and fall back to the update path.

Every cache-miss embed request runs a full synchronous feed poll

perform_retrieve calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline when feed polling is enabled. This downloads and imports the entire RSS feed (creating/revising posts for every item) on each embed request whose URL has no TopicEmbed yet. The 60 s throttle is per embed_url and is bypassed for staff, so distinct URLs (or a staff member) can trigger repeated full feed imports on the worker and heavy writes to the database.

Imported HTML is stored and rendered completely unsanitized

Posts created by TopicEmbed.import use `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and Post#cook returns `raw` verbatim for that method, bypassing PrettyText sanitization entirely. For the RSS path (Jobs::PollFeed) the content is `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)` with no filtering at all, and for import_remote Readability's tag whitelist still allows `<a href>` with arbitrary schemes (e.g. javascript:). A compromised or malicious feed/source therefore yields stored script injection rendered to all users (best.html.erb outputs `raw post.cooked`). Imported HTML should be passed through the sanitizer (e.g. Sanitize/PrettyText whitelist) before being stored.

Loading page reloads forever and re-enqueues a job on every reload

The loading view reloads every 30 seconds indefinitely. Each reload hits EmbedController#best, which, while no TopicEmbed exists, enqueues another RetrieveTopic job. If retrieval permanently fails (invalid host, 404, user not configured), every open embed on the page will keep polling and enqueuing Sidekiq jobs with no backoff or stop condition.

Rails 3 lockfile not updated for new gems

ruby-readability and simple-rss are added to Gemfile and to Gemfile_rails4.lock, but the Rails 3 lockfile (Gemfile.lock, used when RAILS3 is set) is not updated. In deployment/frozen mode Bundler will refuse to boot in Rails 3 mode until the lockfile is regenerated, and the gems will be missing at runtime for `require 'simple-rss'` / `require 'ruby-readability'`.

absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs

The check `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png`. The code then strips all leading slashes and prepends the prefix, producing `http://host/cdn.example.com/img.png`, which is a broken link/image. Protocol-relative URLs are common in feed content and Readability output. Use `URI.join(url, href)` or skip hrefs beginning with `//`.

open-uri fetch of user-influenced URL follows redirects with no timeout (SSRF)

`open(url).read` uses Kernel#open/open-uri on a URL derived from the `embed_url` request parameter. Only the host is validated; open-uri transparently follows HTTP redirects, so the embeddable host (or anyone who can place a redirect on it) can make the Sidekiq worker fetch arbitrary internal URLs. There is also no read/open timeout or size limit, so a slow or huge response ties up the worker. Use an HTTP client with redirect disabled or re-validated, timeouts, and a response size cap.

setnx followed by separate expire can leave a permanent throttle key

The throttle does `$redis.setnx(key)` and then `$redis.expire(key, 60)` as two separate commands. If the worker dies or redis errors between them, the key is created without a TTL and that embed_url is throttled forever for non-staff users (the topic never gets retrieved). Use `SET key 1 NX EX 60` (or setex-style atomic operation).

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
align-items() mixin does not translate values for legacy -webkit-box-align / -ms-flex-align, and emits a non-existent -ms-align-items

The legacy properties `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` use `start`/`end` rather than `flex-start`/`flex-end`, so forwarding `$alignment` unchanged produces invalid declarations for those values (only `center`, `baseline` and `stretch` coincide). `-ms-align-items` is not a property any IE version ever supported and is dead output. Current call sites only use `center` and `baseline`, so nothing breaks today, but the mixin silently fails for other arguments; it should map the values or restrict accepted inputs.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
order() mixin passes the same value to -webkit-box-ordinal-group, which is 1-based unlike `order`

`-webkit-box-ordinal-group` (legacy 2009 flexbox) defaults to 1 and is 1-based, while the standard `order` property defaults to 0. Passing the same `$val` to both means that in legacy-WebKit browsers an item with `order(2)` is given ordinal-group 2 while untouched siblings are at ordinal-group 1, whereas in modern browsers the untouched siblings are at 0. This happens to work for the current usages (2 and 3 are both > default) but the mixin is not a faithful polyfill; a caller using `order(1)` to move an element after its siblings would get no effect in legacy WebKit. Either document the limitation or emit `$val + 1` for the ordinal-group property.

true_positives.matched_candidate:
minimumTokenResponseSchema uses nonsensical computed keys, so sync-mode parsing always fails

`[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` evaluates `ZodString.toString()` which yields the string "[object Object]" as the property name. The resulting schema is `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]": number }` (the second computed key overwrites the first with `z.unknown().optional()`, or vice versa). It does not express "any numeric property is the expiry" at all. Depending on evaluation order the schema either requires a literal `"[object Object]"` number field (all real responses fail → `Invalid refreshed tokens were returned`), or is just `{access_token}` with every other field stripped by zod's default strip behaviour, dropping `expires_in`/`expiry_date` entirely. true_positives.matched_candidate:

`appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError on bad input, `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` throws on a bad ciphertext or when `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is empty, and the handler accepts any HTTP method (a GET with no body reaches `.parse(undefined)`). false_positives.candidate:
Call to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication

The POST to the self-hoster's sync endpoint sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no shared secret, signature or bearer header. The endpoint is expected to return live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary user IDs, so anyone who can reach it can harvest every user's third-party tokens by iterating IDs. Cal.com already has `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` for the reverse direction; the outbound request should at least include it (e.g. in the configured header) so the receiving side can authenticate the caller.

Decrypted payload is stored as the credential key without validation

`keys` is whatever `JSON.parse` returns (could be a string, number, null or array) and is written directly to `credential.key`. A malformed or non-object payload would create a credential that every CalendarService/VideoApiAdapter fails to parse, and the existing `invalid` flag is never reset to `false` when a credential is overwritten with fresh keys, so a previously invalidated credential stays marked invalid even after a successful sync.

In sync mode the O365 expires_in transform is bypassed, so the token is treated as always expired

`refreshTokenResponseSchema` converts the relative `expires_in` seconds into an absolute epoch timestamp, and `getToken` compares that against now via `isExpired(o365AuthCredentials.expires_in)`. When sync is enabled `parseRefreshTokenResponse` uses `minimumTokenResponseSchema` instead, which (if it parses at all) leaves `expires_in` as a small relative number (e.g. 3600). `isExpired(3600)` is always true, so every Graph call triggers a new round-trip to the sync endpoint and a DB write, and the useful error logging that was removed in this diff no longer surfaces malformed responses.

The PR introduces shared logic (`parseRefreshTokenResponse`, `refreshOAuthTokens`) that is now on the token-refresh path of ~10 integrations, plus a new unauthenticated-by-env webhook that writes credentials. The author notes no tests were added. Given the schema-construction bug and the return-shape mismatch above, unit tests for both sync and non-sync branches (and for the webhook's auth / validation / upsert paths) would have caught these before merge.

`prisma` used without being imported

`getClient` now calls `prisma.credential.update(...)` but the file never imports `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma` (imports only include jsforce, rrule, zod, lib helpers and types). This is a TypeScript compile error and, if it slipped through, a `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` at runtime, which would break every Salesforce calendar operation since `getClient` runs in the constructor.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.

Hung/dead flusher processes are never killed because isinstance check against multiprocessing.Process fails for SpawnProcess

`_ensure_processes_alive` now only calls `process.kill()` when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. Previously `self.process.kill()` was called unconditionally. Consequence: when a flusher process is detected as hung (`cause == "hang"`), it is left running while a new process for the same shards is spawned, leading to leaked processes and two flushers concurrently flushing the same Redis shards (duplicate produces to buffered-segments). Use `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)` or `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`.

true_positives.matched_candidate:

getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns resource UUIDs instead of group IDs and never finds per-group resources
